title: BR-045: adopt c^2/10^6 as the published specific_moe unit and align every surface
intent: Owner ruling 2026-08-04 adopted c^2/10^6 as the published scale for TonewoodEntry.specific_moe -- the value its own docstring already claimed and the client's calcSpecificMoe already produced. The backend coded factor was *1e6, returning c^2/10^3, a thousandfold above both. Moving the factor to *1e3 changes one site rather than two. Bounded per the ruling: no scoring redesign, no role targets, no weights, no other index touched. Two stale unit labels surfaced during the mandated consumer sweep and are corrected here because leaving them would perpetuate the exact ambiguity this order settles: StiffnessIndexPanel.vue:158 read 'E/rho x10^6' beside a displayed 24.265 (wrong by 1000x), and router.py:89 documented 'specific_moe (E/rho)' fixing no scale at all.
behavior_change: semantic correction to one derived value. specific_moe now returns ~20-30 for common tonewoods instead of ~20000-30000. Field name, type, nullability and response shape unchanged; computed, never stored, so no migration. Nothing thresholds, sorts or scores on specific_moe -- scorer.py:178 and useTonewoods.ts:67 are pass-through -- so no ranking or recommendation behavior changes. Missing-data behavior (None) and rounding (4dp) unchanged. radiation_ratio, speed_of_sound_computed_m_s, ashby_index and acoustic_impedance_mrayl are untouched.

diff_articulation.what_changed: (1) schemas.py TonewoodEntry.specific_moe: factor *1e6 -> *1e3, and the docstring rewritten to state the ruled unit (c^2/10^6, i.e. (E_GPa/rho)*10^3), the ~20-30 reference range, the fact that nothing scores on it, and the BR-045 provenance. Guard clause, rounding (4dp) and None-return unchanged. (2) router.py:89: OpenAPI description now states the scale and reference range instead of naming the quantity with no unit. (3) StiffnessIndexPanel.vue:158: unit label 'E/rho x10^6' -> 'c^2/10^6'; display text only, no logic change -- the frontend value was already correct, only its label was wrong. (4) test_tonewood_acoustic_indices.py: 4 tests added -- the dimensional identity c^2/1e6 == (E_GPa/rho)*1e3 pinned against a known species, cross-surface parity reproducing the frontend arithmetic across three species, the published reference range, and unchanged missing-data behavior.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Settles the unit authority for a metric the repository published at two scales 1000x apart across backend and client. Not a duplicate of BR-043 (radiation_ratio, a different index whose mismatch collapsed _score_acoustic to 0.0) or BR-044 (frontend radiation-ratio rating collapse, client-local). The parity test is the durable part: it fails if either surface drifts again, which prose docstrings did not prevent.
